The yearly factor is $B = {B}$, and a year is {n} steps of one {per}, so the factor $f$ per {per} satisfies $f^{{n}} = {B}$.
$f = {B}^{1/{n}} \approx {f:num4}$, a change of about **{pct:num2}%** per {per}.
(Dividing {r}% by {n} gives {naive:num2}%, which ignores compounding and is not quite right.)

drills.title: Amount left after a fractional number of half-lives
drills.prompt: A substance has a half-life of {h} hours. A sample starts at {A0} mg. How much remains after {t} hours? Give the answer in mg to 2 decimal places.
drills.solution:
In {t} hours there are $\tfrac{{t}}{{h}} \approx {nh:num4}$ half-lives, so $A = {A0}\left(\tfrac12\right)^{{t}/{h}}$.
$A \approx$ **{A:num2}** mg.

drills.title: Sum of an arithmetic series
drills.prompt: Find the sum of the first {n} terms of the arithmetic sequence ${a1}, {t2}, {t3}, \dots$

drills.title: Sum of a finite geometric series
drills.prompt: Find the sum of the first {n} terms of the geometric sequence ${a1}, {t2}, {t3}, \dots$

drills.title: Sum of an infinite geometric series
drills.prompt: Find the sum of the infinite geometric series ${a1} {t2:signed} {t3:signed} + \cdots$ Give an exact whole number or fraction.
drills.solution:
$a_1 = {a1}$ and $r = \dfrac{{t2}}{{a1}} = {r:texfrac}$. Since $|r| < 1$, the series converges.
$S = \dfrac{a_1}{1 - r} = \dfrac{{a1}}{{omr:texfrac}} =$ **{S:frac}**.

drills.title: z-scores, forward and back
drills.prompt: A data set has mean $\mu = {mu}$ and standard deviation $\sigma = {sd}$. (a) Find the z-score of the value {val}. (b) Which value has z-score {z2}?
drills.solution:
(a) $z = \dfrac{\text{value} - \mu}{\sigma} = \dfrac{{val} - {mu}}{{sd}} = \dfrac{{d}}{{sd}} =$ **{z}**.
(b) Go back with $\text{value} = \mu + z\sigma = {mu} + ({z2})({sd}) = {mu} + ({shift}) =$ **{x2}**.

drills.title: The 68–95–99.7 rule
drills.prompt: Values are approximately normal with mean {mu} and standard deviation {sd}. Using the 68–95–99.7 rule, about what percent of the values lie between {xl} and {xh}?
drills.solution:
Standardize the ends: {xl} is $z = {lo}$ and {xh} is $z = {hi}$.
By the rule (bands of 0.15%, 2.35%, 13.5%, 34%, 34%, 13.5%, 2.35%, 0.15% from left to right), about {cl}% of values lie below $z = {lo}$ and {ch}% lie below $z = {hi}$.
Between them: ${ch}\% - {cl}\% =$ **{pct}%**.

drills.title: Normal percents from a z-table
drills.prompt: Measurements are approximately normal with mean {mu} and standard deviation {sd}. What percent of the measurements are {dir} {val}? Use a z-table or technology, and give the percent to 1 decimal place.
drills.solution:
$z = \dfrac{{val} - {mu}}{{sd}} = {z}$. The area to the left of $z = {z}$ is about {left}%.
That is the percent below {val}; the percent above it is 100% minus that. The question asks for {dir}, so the answer is about **{pct}%**.

drills.title: Overall rate as a weighted average
drills.prompt: A treatment succeeded for {s1} of {n1} patients with mild cases ({p1}%) and {s2} of {n2} patients with severe cases ({p2}%). What is its overall success rate? Give a percent to 1 decimal place.
drills.solution:
Add the successes and the patients: $\dfrac{{s1} + {s2}}{{n1} + {n2}} = \dfrac{{stot}}{{tot}} \approx$ **{rate}%**.
As a weighted average: a fraction $\tfrac{{n1}}{{tot}} \approx {w}$ of the patients are mild cases, so the overall rate lies between {p2}% and {p1}%, pulled toward the larger group. (The unweighted average, {naive}%, is wrong because the groups differ in size.)

drills.title: Expected count with no association

calc.ex: round((a + b)*(a + c)/(a + b + c + d), 1)
calc.gap: round(a - round((a + b)*(a + c)/(a + b + c + d), 1), 1)

drills.prompt:
A survey recorded whether people walk to work.

| | Walk | Don't walk | Total |
|---|---|---|---|
| City | {a} | {b} | {r1} |
| Suburb | {c} | {d} | {r2} |
| Total | {k1} | {k2} | {N} |

If where people live and walking to work were not associated, what count would you expect in the City/Walk cell (1 decimal place)? What is the observed count minus that expected count?
drills.solution:
Expected count $= \dfrac{\text{row total} \times \text{column total}}{\text{grand total}} = \dfrac{{r1} \times {k1}}{{N}} = \dfrac{{prod:dp0}}{{N}} \approx$ **{ex}**.
Observed − expected $= {a} - {ex} =$ **{gap}**. (A positive gap means more city residents walk than "no association" predicts; a negative gap, fewer.)

drills.title: Least-squares line by hand
drills.prompt: Find the least-squares line $\hat y = bx + a$ for the points $({x1}, {y1})$, $({x2}, {y2})$, $({x3}, {y3})$, $({x4}, {y4})$, $({x5}, {y5})$.
drills.solution:
Means: $\bar x = {xbar}$ and $\bar y = \tfrac{{ysum}}{5} = {ybar}$.
The $x$-deviations are $-2, -1, 0, 1, 2$, so $\sum d_x^2 = 4 + 1 + 0 + 1 + 4 = 10$, and $\sum d_x d_y = -2({y1}) - 1({y2}) + 0({y3}) + 1({y4}) + 2({y5}) = {sxy}$. (Multiplying by $y - \bar y$ instead of $y$ gives the same sum, because the $x$-deviations add to 0.)
Slope: $b = \dfrac{{sxy}}{10} =$ **{slope}**. Intercept: $a = \bar y - b\bar x = {ybar} - ({slope})({xbar}) = {ybar} - ({bx}) =$ **{icpt}**.

drills.title: Least-squares line from summary statistics
drills.prompt: For a data set, $\bar x = {xbar}$, $\bar y = {ybar}$, $\sigma_x = {sx}$, $\sigma_y = {sy}$ and $r = {r}$. Find the slope $b$ and intercept $a$ of the least-squares line $\hat y = bx + a$, and the predicted $\hat y$ at $x = {xp}$.
drills.solution:
Slope: $b = r\dfrac{\sigma_y}{\sigma_x} = {r} \times \dfrac{{sy}}{{sx}} =$ **{slope}**.
The line passes through $(\bar x, \bar y)$: $a = \bar y - b\bar x = {ybar} - ({bxbar}) =$ **{icpt}**.
Prediction: $\hat y = {slope}({xp}) + ({icpt}) = {bxp} + ({icpt}) =$ **{yp}**.

drills.title: r-squared from squared residuals
drills.prompt: For a data set, the total variation is $\sum (y - \bar y)^2 = {sst}$, and the least-squares line has sum of squared residuals $\text{SSE} = {sse}$. Its slope is {sgn}. Find $r^2$, and find $r$ to 3 decimal places.
drills.solution:
$r^2 = 1 - \dfrac{\text{SSE}}{\sum (y - \bar y)^2} = 1 - \dfrac{{sse}}{{sst}} = 1 - {ratio} =$ **{r2}**.
$|r| = \sqrt{{r2}}$, and $r$ has the same sign as the slope ({sgn}), so $r \approx$ **{r:dp3}**.

drills.title: Repeating decimal to fraction
drills.prompt: Write $0.\overline{{n}}$ as a fraction in lowest terms.
drills.solution:
Let $x = 0.\overline{{n}}$. The block has 2 digits, so $100x = {n}.\overline{{n}}$.
Subtract: $100x - x = {n}$, so $99x = {n}$ and $x = \dfrac{{n}}{99}$.
The greatest common factor of {n} and 99 is {g}, so in lowest terms $x =$ **$\dfrac{{num}}{{den}}$**.

drills.title: Decimal with a delayed repeat to fraction
drills.prompt: Write $0.{a}\overline{{b}} = 0.{a}{b}{b}{b}\ldots$ as a fraction in lowest terms.
drills.solution:
Let $x = 0.{a}{b}{b}{b}\ldots$ Then $10x = {a}.{b}{b}{b}\ldots$ and $100x = {big}.{b}{b}{b}\ldots$
Subtract: $100x - 10x = {big} - {a}$, so $90x = {top}$ and $x = \dfrac{{top}}{90}$.
The greatest common factor of {top} and 90 is {g}, so in lowest terms $x =$ **$\dfrac{{num}}{{den}}$**.

drills.title: Two workers together
drills.prompt: One machine finishes a job in {ta} hours and a second machine finishes the same job in {tb} hours. Working together, how many hours do they need? Give an exact fraction or a decimal rounded to 2 decimal places.
drills.solution:
Rates add: $\dfrac{t}{{ta}} + \dfrac{t}{{tb}} = 1$.
Multiply by {lcd}: ${ca}t + {cb}t = {lcd}$, so ${csum}t = {lcd}$ and $t = \dfrac{{lcd}}{{csum}} \approx$ **{together:num2}** hours.

drills.title: Round-trip average speed
drills.prompt: You drive {dist} miles at {sa} mph and return the same {dist} miles at {sb} mph. What is your average speed for the round trip, in mph?
drills.solution:
Time out: $\dfrac{{dist}}{{sa}} = {t1}$ h. Time back: $\dfrac{{dist}}{{sb}} = {t2}$ h. Total: {d2} miles in {tt} hours.
Average speed $= \dfrac{{d2}}{{tt}} =$ **{avg}** mph. (Check with the harmonic mean: $\dfrac{2 \cdot {sa} \cdot {sb}}{{sa} + {sb}} = {avg}$.)

drills.title: Final exam score needed
drills.prompt: A course grade counts homework 20%, tests 50% and the final exam 30%. Your homework average is {hw} and your test average is {ts}. What final exam score gives a course grade of exactly {goal}?
drills.solution:
Weighted average: $0.20({hw}) + 0.50({ts}) + 0.30F = {goal}$.
So ${phw} + {pts} + 0.30F = {goal}$, which gives $0.30F = {need:num1}$ and $F =$ **{fin}**.

drills.title: Absolute value equal to a variable expression
drills.prompt: Solve $|x {a:signed}| = {b}x$. Check for extraneous solutions, then enter the solution as an integer or exact fraction.
drills.solution:
Split: $x {a:signed} = {b}x$ gives $x = {c1:texfrac}$, and $x {a:signed} = -{b}x$ gives $x = {c2:texfrac}$.
The right side ${b}x$ equals a distance, so it must be at least 0, which needs $x \ge 0$. The candidate ${bad:texfrac}$ is negative, so it is extraneous (the left side is positive there, the right side negative).
The solution is $x =$ **${ans:texfrac}$**.

drills.title: Sum of two absolute values
drills.prompt: Solve $|x {np:signed}| + |x {nq:signed}| = {s}$. Enter both solutions, smaller first.
drills.solution:
The critical values are {p} and {q}, which split the line into three regions.
For $x < {p}$, both insides are negative: the sum is $-2x {pq:signed}$. Setting $-2x {pq:signed} = {s}$ gives $x = {lo}$, which is in this region.
For ${p} \le x < {q}$, the sum is always ${q} - ({p}) = {d}$, which is not {s}, so there are no solutions here.
For $x \ge {q}$, the sum is $2x {npq:signed}$. Setting it equal to {s} gives $x = {hi}$, which is in this region.
Solutions: **{lo}** and **{hi}**. (Distance check: each is {ov} beyond the nearer critical value, and ${d} + 2({ov}) = {s}$.)

drills.title: Interval to absolute value inequality
drills.prompt: Write ${a} \le x \le {b}$ in the form $|x - m| \le h$. Enter $m$ and $h$.
drills.solution:
The midpoint is $m = \dfrac{ {a} + ({b}) }{2} =$ **{m}**, and the half-width is $h = \dfrac{ {b} - ({a}) }{2} =$ **{h}**.
So the interval is $|x {nm:signed}| \le {h}$.

drills.title: Error through a linear formula
drills.prompt: A quantity is computed as $y = {k}x {b:signed}$. (a) If $x$ is measured as {x0} with an error of at most {delta:num4}, what is the largest possible error in $y$? (b) How close to {x0} must $x$ be to guarantee that $y$ is within {eps:num4} of {y0}?
drills.solution:
Near $x = {x0}$, $y = {y0}$, and $|y {ny0:signed}| = |{k}(x - {x0})| = {ak}\,|x - {x0}|$.
(a) With $|x - {x0}| \le {delta:num4}$: the error in $y$ is at most ${ak} \times {delta:num4} =$ **{err:num4}**.
(b) Need ${ak}\,|x - {x0}| \le {eps:num4}$, so $|x - {x0}| \le {eps:num4} \div {ak} =$ **{del2:num4}**.

drills.title: Evaluate an inverse function
drills.prompt: Let $f(x) = {a:coef}x {b:signed}$. Find $f^{-1}({c})$. (Give an exact fraction if it isn't a whole number.)
drills.solution:
$f^{-1}({c})$ is the input whose output is {c}, so solve $f(x) = {c}$:
${a:coef}x {b:signed} = {c}$, so ${a:coef}x = {c} {nb:signed} = {cb}$ and $x = \dfrac{ {cb} }{ {a} } =$ **${ans:texfrac}$**.
Check: ${a}\left({ans:texfrac}\right) {b:signed} = {cb} {b:signed} = {c}$.

drills.title: Find the inverse of a linear function
drills.prompt: Let $f(x) = {a:coef}x {b:signed}$. Find a formula for $f^{-1}(x)$.
drills.solution:
Write $y = {a:coef}x {b:signed}$ and swap $x$ and $y$: $x = {a:coef}y {b:signed}$.
Solve for $y$: ${a:coef}y = x {nb:signed}$, so **$f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{x {nb:signed}}{ {a} }$**.
The inverse undoes the steps of $f$ in reverse order: $f$ multiplies by ${a}$ and then adds ${b}$, so $f^{-1}$ subtracts ${b}$ and then divides by ${a}$.

drills.title: Work backward through a data plan
drills.prompt: A phone plan costs {F:money0} a month and includes {G} GB of data. Each GB beyond {G} GB costs {r:money0}, charged in proportion to the amount used. One month's bill is {B:money}. How many GB of data were used?
drills.solution:
The model is $C(g) = {F}$ for $0 \le g \le {G}$ and $C(g) = {F} + {r}(g - {G})$ for $g > {G}$.
The bill is more than {F:money0}, so the second piece applies: ${F} + {r}(g - {G}) = {B}$.
Then ${r}(g - {G}) = {extra}$, so $g - {G} = {e}$ and $g =$ **{u}** GB. (It is more than {G}, as the second piece requires.)

drills.title: Choose a constant to make a piecewise function continuous
drills.prompt: For what value of $k$ is $f(x) = \begin{cases} {m:coef}x {b:signed}, & x < {c} \\ kx {d:signed}, & x \ge {c} \end{cases}$ continuous? (Give an exact fraction if it isn't a whole number.)
drills.solution:
The only possible break is at the breakpoint $x = {c}$. There the first formula gives ${m}({c}) {b:signed} = {v}$, and the second gives ${c}k {d:signed}$.
Set them equal: ${c}k {d:signed} = {v}$, so ${c}k = {v} {nd:signed} = {vd}$ and $k =$ **${k:texfrac}$**.

drills.title: Tax under a bracket schedule

calc.marg: if(x < B1, r1, if(x < B2, r2, r3))

drills.prompt: A (made-up) tax schedule charges {r1}% on income up to {B1:money0}, {r2}% on income from {B1:money0} to {B2:money0}, and {r3}% on income over {B2:money0}. For an income of {x:money0}, find the total tax and the average tax rate as a percent (1 decimal place).
drills.solution:
Split the income into layers and tax each at its own rate:
first layer {L1:money0} × {r1}% = {t1:money}; second layer {L2:money0} × {r2}% = {t2:money}; top layer {L3:money0} × {r3}% = {t3:money}.
Total tax: **{T:money}**. Average rate: {T:money} ÷ {x:money0} × 100 ≈ **{avgp:dp1}%**. (The marginal rate, on the next dollar, is {marg}%.)

drills.title: Average rate of change of a quadratic
drills.prompt: Find the average rate of change of $f(x) = {a:coef}x^2 {b:signedcoef}x {c:signed}$ from $x = {p}$ to $x = {q}$.
drills.solution:
$f({p}) = {fp}$ and $f({q}) = {fq}$, so the average rate is $\dfrac{ {fq} - ({fp}) }{ {q} - ({p}) } = \dfrac{ {dy} }{ {w} } =$ **{arc}**.
Shortcut for quadratics: $a(p + q) + b = {a}({s}) + ({b}) = {arc}$.

drills.title: Equation of a secant line
drills.prompt: Find the equation of the secant line of $f(x) = {a:coef}x^2 {b:signedcoef}x {c:signed}$ through the points where $x = {p}$ and $x = {q}$. Write it in slope-intercept form.
drills.solution:
The points are $({p}, {fp})$ and $({q}, {fq})$. Slope: $\dfrac{ {fq} - ({fp}) }{ {q} - ({p}) } = \dfrac{ {dy} }{ {w} } = {m}$.
Point-slope form through $({p}, {fp})$: $y - ({fp}) = {m}(x - ({p}))$. Then $y = {m:coef}x - ({mp}) + ({fp})$, which simplifies to **$y = {m:coef}x {k:signed}$**.
Check the other point: ${m}({q}) {k:signed} = {fq}$.

drills.title: Simplify a difference quotient
drills.prompt: Let $f(x) = {a:coef}x^2 {b:signedcoef}x {c:signed}$. Simplify the difference quotient $\dfrac{f({p} + h) - f({p})}{h}$ for $h \ne 0$.
drills.solution:
Expand: $f({p} + h) = {a:coef}({p} + h)^2 + ({b})({p} + h) {c:signed} = {fp} {s0:signedcoef}h {a:signedcoef}h^2$, since the terms without $h$ add up to $f({p}) = {fp}$.
Subtract $f({p}) = {fp}$: ${s0:coef}h {a:signedcoef}h^2$. Divide by $h$: **${s0} {a:signedcoef}h$**.
As $h$ gets close to 0 this approaches {lim}, the instantaneous rate of change of $f$ at $x = {p}$.

drills.title: Evaluate a 2 × 2 determinant
drills.prompt: Evaluate the determinant $\begin{vmatrix} {a} & {b} \\ {c} & {d} \end{vmatrix}$.
drills.solution: Main diagonal product minus the other diagonal product: $({a})({d}) - ({b})({c}) = {ad} - ({bc}) =$ **{det}**.

drills.title: Solve a system by Cramer's rule
drills.prompt:
Solve by Cramer's rule. Give $D$, $D_x$ and $D_y$, then the solution.

$$\begin{cases} {a:coef}x {b:signedcoef}y = {e} \\ {c:coef}x {d:signedcoef}y = {f} \end{cases}$$
drills.solution:
$D = ({a})({d}) - ({b})({c}) = {ad} - ({bc}) =$ **{det}**.
Replace the $x$-column with the constants: $D_x = ({e})({d}) - ({b})({f}) = {ed} - ({bf}) =$ **{dx}**.
Replace the $y$-column: $D_y = ({a})({f}) - ({e})({c}) = {af} - ({ec}) =$ **{dy}**.
So $x = D_x / D = {dx} / ({det}) =$ **{xs}** and $y = D_y / D = {dy} / ({det}) =$ **{ys}**.

drills.title: When a system has no unique solution
drills.prompt: For which value of $k$ does the system $\;kx {b:signedcoef}y = {e}$, $\;{c:coef}x {d:signedcoef}y = {f}\;$ fail to have exactly one solution?
drills.solution:
The coefficient determinant is $D = k({d}) - ({b})({c}) = {d:coef}k - ({bc})$.
There is exactly one solution unless $D = 0$: ${d:coef}k = {bc}$, so $k =$ **{kk}**.
For that $k$ the lines have the same slope, so the system has no solution or infinitely many; $D_x$ and $D_y$ tell which.

drills.title: Minimize cost over an unbounded region
drills.prompt: Minimize $C = {p:coef}x {q:signedcoef}y$ subject to $x \ge 0$, $y \ge 0$, ${a1:coef}x {b1:signedcoef}y \ge {c1}$ and ${a2:coef}x {b2:signedcoef}y \ge {c2}$. What is the minimum value of $C$?
drills.solution:
The region is unbounded (it goes on up and to the right), but $C$ has positive coefficients and $x, y \ge 0$, so $C$ can't keep decreasing: the minimum is at a vertex.
The vertices are $(0, {yi})$, $({x0}, {y0})$ (where the two slanted lines meet) and $({xi}, 0)$.
$C$ there: ${C1}$, ${C2}$ and ${C3}$. The smallest is **{best}**. (There is no maximum.)

drills.title: How far can a profit change? (sensitivity)
drills.prompt: The feasible region $x \ge 0$, $y \ge 0$, ${a1:coef}x {b1:signedcoef}y \le {c1}$, ${a2:coef}x {b2:signedcoef}y \le {c2}$ has a vertex at $({x0}, {y0})$. You want to maximize $P = px + {q}y$. For which values of $p$ is $({x0}, {y0})$ a best vertex? Give the smallest and the largest such $p$.
drills.solution:
At $({x0}, {y0})$ two edges meet: one along ${a2:coef}x {b2:signedcoef}y = {c2}$, with slope $-\tfrac{{a2}}{{b2}}$, and one along ${a1:coef}x {b1:signedcoef}y = {c1}$, with slope $-\tfrac{{a1}}{{b1}}$.
The level lines of $P$ have slope $-\tfrac{p}{{q}}$. The vertex is best when that slope lies between the edge slopes: $\tfrac{{a2}}{{b2}} \le \tfrac{p}{{q}} \le \tfrac{{a1}}{{b1}}$.
Multiply by {q}: **{lo}** $\le p \le$ **{hi}**.

drills.title: Synthetic division by x − c
drills.prompt: Use synthetic division to divide $\;{a3:coef}x^3 {a2:signedcoef}x^2 {a1:signedcoef}x {a0:signed}\;$ by $\;x {mc:signed}$. Give the quotient and the remainder.
drills.solution:
The divisor is $x - ({cz})$, so $c = {cz}$. Write the coefficients ${a3}, {a2}, {a1}, {a0}$.
Bring down {a3}. Then multiply by {cz} and add, column by column: ${a2} + ({p1}) = {q1}$; ${a1} + ({p2}) = {q0}$; ${a0} + ({p3}) = {r}$.
Quotient **${q2:coef}x^2 {q1:signedcoef}x {q0:signed}$**, remainder **{r}**.

drills.title: Remainder theorem
drills.prompt: Find the remainder when $P(x) = {a3:coef}x^3 {a2:signedcoef}x^2 {a1:signedcoef}x {a0:signed}$ is divided by $x {mc:signed}$.
drills.solution:
By the remainder theorem, the remainder on dividing by $x - ({cz})$ is $P({cz})$:
$P({cz}) = {a3:coef}({cz})^3 + ({a2})({cz})^2 + ({a1})({cz}) + ({a0}) = {t3} + ({t2}) + ({t1}) + ({a0}) =$ **{rem}**.

drills.title: Find the other zeros of a cubic
drills.prompt: $x = {r1}$ is a zero of $P(x) = x^3 {b2:signedcoef}x^2 {b1:signedcoef}x {b0:signed}$. Divide out the factor it gives, then find the other two zeros (smaller one first).
drills.solution:
By the factor theorem, $x - ({r1})$ is a factor. Synthetic division with $c = {r1}$ on $1, {b2}, {b1}, {b0}$ leaves remainder 0 and quotient $x^2 {s1:signedcoef}x {s0:signed}$.
Factor the quadratic: product {s0}, sum {s1}, so $(x {m2:signed})(x {m3:signed})$.
The other zeros are **{r2}** and **{r3}**.

drills.title: One coefficient of a binomial power
drills.prompt: Find the coefficient of $x^{{kk}}$ in the expansion of $({p:coef}x {q:signed})^{{nn}}$.
drills.solution:
With $a = {p:coef}x$ and $b = {q}$, the term containing $x^{{kk}}$ has $a^{{kk}}$ and $b^{{j}}$:
$\dbinom{{nn}}{{j}}({p:coef}x)^{{kk}}({q})^{{j}} = {bc} \cdot {pk} \cdot ({qj})\,x^{{kk}}$.
The coefficient is **{coef}**.

drills.title: Binomial coefficients
drills.prompt: Compute $\dbinom{{nn}}{{kk}}$, the entry in row {nn}, position {kk} of Pascal's triangle (counting rows and positions from 0).
drills.solution:
$\dbinom{{nn}}{{kk}} = \dfrac{{nn}!}{{kk}!\,{nk}!} =$ **{val}**.
Check with Pascal's rule: it is the sum of the two entries above it, $\dbinom{{nm1}}{{km1}} + \dbinom{{nm1}}{{kk}} = {up1} + {up2} = {val}$.

drills.title: Pythagorean triples from Euclid's formula
drills.prompt: Use Euclid's formula with $m = {m}$ and $n = {n}$ to make a Pythagorean triple $m^2 - n^2$, $2mn$, $m^2 + n^2$.

drills.title: Sum and product of the roots
drills.prompt: Without solving, find the sum and the product of the two real roots of $\;{a:coef}x^2 {b:signedcoef}x {c:signed} = 0$. Give exact fractions.
drills.solution:
Here $a = {a}$, $b = {b}$, $c = {c}$, and $b^2 - 4ac = {D} > 0$, so there are two real roots.
Sum: $-\dfrac{\,b}{\,a} = -\dfrac{{b}}{{a}} =$ **${S:texfrac}$**. Product: $\dfrac{\,c}{\,a} = \dfrac{{c}}{{a}} =$ **${P:texfrac}$**.

drills.title: Symmetric expressions of the roots
drills.prompt: Let $r$ and $s$ be the roots of $x^2 {b:signedcoef}x {c:signed} = 0$. Without solving, find $r^2 + s^2$ and $\dfrac1r + \dfrac1s$ (exact fraction).
drills.solution:
The discriminant is ${D} > 0$, so the roots are real. Sum $S = -b = {S}$, product $P = c = {c}$.
$r^2 + s^2 = S^2 - 2P = {S2} - ({twoc}) =$ **{sq}**.
$\dfrac1r + \dfrac1s = \dfrac{r + s}{rs} = \dfrac{\,S}{\,P} = \dfrac{{S}}{{c}} =$ **${rec:texfrac}$**.

drills.title: One root given, find the other
drills.prompt: One root of $x^2 + kx {c:signed} = 0$ is ${m}$. Find the other root and $k$.
drills.solution:
The product of the roots is ${c}$: ${m} \cdot s = {c}$, so the other root is $s =$ **{n}**.
The sum of the roots is $-k$: ${m} + ({n}) = {sum}$, so $k =$ **{k}**.
Check: $(x {nm:signed})(x {nn:signed})$ expands to $x^2 {k:signedcoef}x {c:signed}$.

drills.title: Solve x² + bx + c < 0
drills.prompt: The solution of $x^2 {b:signedcoef}x {c:signed} {sym} 0$ is the interval between two numbers $p$ and $q$ (with $p < q$). Find $p$ and $q$.
drills.solution:
Factor: $x^2 {b:signedcoef}x {c:signed} = (x {np:signed})(x {nq:signed})$, so the roots are ${p}$ and ${q}$.
The parabola opens up, so it is below the $x$-axis between its roots. So $p =$ **{p}** and $q =$ **{q}** (endpoints included only for $\le$).

drills.title: Solve ax² + bx + c ≥ 0
drills.prompt: Solve $\;{A}x^2 {B:signedcoef}x {C:signed} \ge 0$. The solution has the form $x \le p$ or $x \ge q$. Give $p$ and $q$ as exact fractions.
drills.solution:
Factor: $({u:coef}x {v:signed})({r:coef}x {w:signed}) \ge 0$. The boundary points are ${x1:texfrac}$ and ${x2:texfrac}$.
The leading coefficient {A} is positive, so the parabola is at or above the axis outside its roots: $x \le$ **${lo:texfrac}$** or $x \ge$ **${hi:texfrac}$**.

drills.title: When is a projectile above a given height?
drills.prompt: A ball's height in feet is $h(t) = -16t^2 + {v}t + {h0}$, $t$ seconds after it is thrown. During which time interval is the ball higher than {H} feet? Give the start and end times in seconds.
drills.solution:
Solve $-16t^2 + {v}t + {h0} > {H}$: subtract {H} to get $-16t^2 + {v}t + ({h0} - {H}) > 0$. Divide by $-16$ and reverse the symbol: $t^2 - {s}t + {pr} < 0$.
The roots are $t = {t1}$ and $t = {t2}$ (their sum is {s} and product {pr}), and the upward parabola $t^2 - {s}t + {pr}$ is negative between them.
The ball is above {H} ft from $t =$ **{t1}** to $t =$ **{t2}** s.

drills.title: Complete the square the al-Khwarizmi way
drills.prompt: "A square and {b} roots equal {c}": $x^2 + {b}x = {c}$. Following al-Khwarizmi, what number do you add to both sides to complete the square, and what is the positive solution?
drills.solution:
Halve the roots: $\tfrac{{b}}{2} = {h}$. Square it: **{sq}**. Add it to both sides: $x^2 + {b}x + {sq} = {c} + {sq} = {tot}$, that is $(x + {h})^2 = {tot}$.
The square root of {tot} is {side}, so $x + {h} = {side}$ and $x =$ **{r}**. (The negative root, $x = -{side} - {h} = {neg}$, was not considered: a side can't be negative.)

drills.title: Cut a segment in the golden ratio
drills.prompt: A segment {L} cm long is cut in the golden ratio, so that $\dfrac{\text{whole}}{\text{longer}} = \dfrac{\text{longer}}{\text{shorter}}$. Find the lengths of the longer and shorter parts, to 2 decimal places.
drills.solution:
Let the longer part be $x$: $\dfrac{{L}}{x} = \dfrac{x}{{L} - x}$, so $x^2 = {L}({L} - x)$ and $x^2 + {L}x - {L}^2 = 0$.
The positive root is $x = \dfrac{-{L} + \sqrt{{L}^2 + 4 \cdot {L}^2}}{2} = \dfrac{{L}(\sqrt5 - 1)}{2} = \dfrac{{L}}{\varphi}$, so the longer part is **{long:num2}** cm and the shorter part is ${L} - x \approx$ **{short:num2}** cm.
